title: ⚔️ Chapter Boss ⭐⭐⭐: The Night of the New Year

questions.prompt: Amine tells a friend about his cousin's afternoon. Which of these sentences is correct?

options.text: Yesterday, she plays with her cousins.
Yesterday, she played with her cousins.
Yesterday, she playeds with her cousins.
Yesterday, she will play with her cousins.

questions.explanation: Yesterday calls the simple past, and a regular verb takes -ed for every subject: she played. The form "plays" stays in the present, "playeds" keeps the -s that belongs to the present only, and "will play" sends the action to the future, which yesterday forbids.

questions.prompt: Complete both blanks: "Children ___ the right to education, and every child ___ the right to a home."
questions.explanation: Children are several, that is they, so the verb is have; every child is one child, that is he or she, so the verb is has. The three other pairs give at least one of the two subjects the verb of the other, and the words the right to never change the verb in front of them.

questions.prompt: What is the simple past of the verb hug?
questions.explanation: The verb hug is short and ends in one vowel plus one consonant, so the consonant doubles before the ending: hugged. The spelling "huged" forgets the doubling, "hugeed" invents an e the verb does not have, and "huggd" drops the e of the ending itself.

questions.prompt: Complete both blanks: "Last week, my sister ___ a card and ___ a cake for our teacher."
questions.explanation: Both verbs are irregular and change shape: write becomes wrote and make becomes made. The forms "writed" and "maked" add the regular ending to verbs that never take it, and the two mixed pairs get one verb right and the other wrong.

questions.prompt: Complete both blanks: "I ___ surprised, and my parents ___ very happy."
questions.explanation: The past of be chooses its shape from the subject: I, he, she and it take was, while you, we and they take were. So it is was for I and were for my parents, and every other pair puts at least one subject on the wrong line.

questions.prompt: Karim tells the class about the New Year party at his house. Which of these sentences is completely correct?

options.text: Last night we blew up the balloons and we put on our best clothes.
Last night we blowed up the balloons and we put on our best clothes.
Last night we blew up the balloons and we putted on our best clothes.
Last night we blow up the balloons and we put on our best clothes.

questions.explanation: Last night is over, so both verbs go to the past, and both are irregular: blow up becomes blew up, and put does not change at all. The form "blowed up" adds the regular ending to the first verb, "putted" adds it to the second, and the last sentence leaves both verbs in the present.
